note: One entry per clip. 'segments' is the narration: one line per on-screen caption, in the order the captions appear in the scene.

segments.caption: A model cannot know your hospital's own protocols.
segments.text: A language model learns from public text, so it cannot know your hospital's own protocols. Asked when antibiotics must start under our sepsis protocol, it says three hours: a reasonable national figure, but not our rule.

segments.caption: Split the documents into chunks and embed each chunk once.
segments.text: Retrieval starts by splitting the hospital's documents into chunks. Almanac used chunks of one thousand tokens. Each chunk is embedded once into a vector, which in Almanac had one thousand five hundred thirty-six numbers.

segments.caption: Embed the question and score every chunk by cosine similarity.
segments.text: At question time, the question is embedded the same way and compared with every chunk by co-sine similarity. Here the three best chunks score zero point eight six, zero point seven nine, and zero point six two.

segments.caption: Only chunks above a threshold pass: Almanac used λ = 0.83.
segments.text: Only chunks that score above a threshold are passed on. Almanac used a threshold, lambda, of zero point eight three, so here only the first chunk, from the sepsis protocol, passes.

segments.caption: If nothing passes, the published Almanac falls back on the model's own knowledge.
segments.text: A second question, about rattlesnake bites, finds no good match: its best score is only zero point seven one. The published Almanac then falls back on the model's own knowledge. The preprint version abstained instead, and said the answer was not found in the sources.

segments.caption: The passing chunk goes into the prompt with its source, and the answer cites it.
segments.text: The passing chunk is pasted into the prompt, together with its source. The model now answers within one hour, which is what the synthetic protocol says, and it cites section two of that protocol.

segments.caption: Almanac ranked first of four systems on 314 clinical questions.
segments.text: Clinicians compared Almanac with Chat G P T four, Bing, and Bard on three hundred fourteen clinical questions. Almanac ranked first for factuality, completeness, and preference, and its citations were correct ninety-one percent of the time.

segments.caption: Read with care: the adversarial wins come mostly from declining to answer.
segments.text: Read these results with care. Against adversarial prompts, Almanac scored one hundred percent and Chat G P T four seven percent, mostly because Almanac declined to answer. The questions and the grading came from the study's own clinicians, and only twenty-five questions are public.
